# f5xc_tcp_loadbalancer (Resource)

TCP load balancer view defines a required parameters that can be used in CRUD, to create and manage TCP load balancer.<br>It can be used to create TCP load balancer and TCP load balancer with SNI.<br><br>View will create following child objects.<br><br>* Virtual-host<br>* default route<br>* clusters<br>* endpoints<br>* advertise policy

To get more information about f5xc_tcp_loadbalancer, refer:

- [API documentation](https://docs.cloud.f5.com/docs-v2/api/views-tcp-loadbalancer)

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Example: Tcp Loadbalancer - Basic

resource "f5xc_origin_pool" "example" {
  name                   = "example-tcp-lb-uh3812y3-op"
  namespace              = "terraform-acceptance-test"
  loadbalancer_algorithm = ["ROUND_ROBIN"]
  endpoint_selection     = ["LOCAL_PREFERRED"]

  port_choice = {
    port = 443
  }

  origin_servers = [
    {
      choice = {
        public_name = {
          dns_name = "example.com"
        }
      }
    }
  ]

  tls_choice = {
    no_tls = true
  }

  upstream_conn_pool_reuse_type = {
    map_downstream_to_upstream_conn_pool_type_choice = {
      disable_conn_pool_reuse = true
    }
  }
}



resource "f5xc_tcp_loadbalancer" "example" {
  name      = "example-tcp-lb-uh3812y3"
  namespace = "terraform-acceptance-test"
  domains   = ["example-tcp-lb-uh3812y3.example.com", "alt-example-tcp-lb-uh3812y3.example.com"]

  origin_pools_weights = [
    {
      pool_choice = {
        pool = {
          name      = f5xc_origin_pool.example.name
          namespace = f5xc_origin_pool.example.namespace
        }
      }
    }
  ]

  port_choice = {
    port_ranges = "24110,24111"
  }

  sni_default_lb_choice = {
    default_lb_with_sni = true
  }

  advertise_choice = {
    advertise_on_public_default_vip = true
  }

  hash_policy_choice = {
    hash_policy_choice_least_active = true
  }

  cluster_retract_choice = {
    retract_cluster = true
  }

  loadbalancer_type_choice = {
    tcp = true
  }

  service_policy_choice = {
    service_policies_from_namespace = true
  }

  description = "acceptance test tcp loadbalancer"
  labels = {
    env  = "example"
    team = "edge"
  }
  annotations = {
    owner = "platform-team"
  }
  idle_timeout = 2000
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `loadbalancer_type_choice` (Attributes) Proxy choice The type of load balancer, can be 'tcp', 'tls_tcp' or 'tls_tcp_auto_cert'<br>Exactly one of `tcp`, `tls_tcp`, or `tls_tcp_auto_cert` must be specified. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice))
- `name` (String) name This is the name of configuration object. It has to be unique within the namespace. It can only be specified during create API and cannot be changed during replace API. The value of name has to follow DNS-1035 format.
- `namespace` (String) namespace This defines the workspace within which each the configuration object is to be created. Must be a DNS_LABEL format. For a namespace object itself, namespace value will be ''
- `origin_pools_weights` (Attributes List) Origin Pools with Weights Origin pools and weights used for this load balancer. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--origin_pools_weights))
- `port_choice` (Attributes) Listen Port Listen Port for this load balancer<br>Exactly one of `listen_port` or `port_ranges` must be specified. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--port_choice))

### Optional

- `advertise_choice` (Attributes) Advertise choice This is a choice to select method to advertise VIP.<br>Exactly one of `advertise_custom`, `advertise_on_public`, `advertise_on_public_default_vip`, or `do_not_advertise` must be specified when `advertise_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--advertise_choice))
- `annotations` (Map of String) annotations Annotations is an unstructured key value map stored with a resource that may be set by external tools to store and retrieve arbitrary metadata. They are not queryable and should be preserved when modifying objects.
- `cluster_retract_choice` (Attributes) Oneof for Cluster retraction Specifies whether retraction of cluster has to be enabled or disabled<br>Exactly one of `do_not_retract_cluster` or `retract_cluster` must be specified when `cluster_retract_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--cluster_retract_choice))
- `description` (String) description Human readable description for the object
- `dns_volterra_managed` (Boolean) Manage DNS Domain DNS records for domains will be managed automatically by Volterra. This requires the domain to be delegated to F5XC using the Delegated Domain feature.<br>**Default:** `false`
- `domains` (List of String) Domains A list of Domains (host/authority header) that will be matched to this Load Balancer. Supported Domains and search order: 1. Exact Domain names: www.foo.com. 2. Domains starting with a Wildcard: *.foo.com. Not supported Domains: - Just a Wildcard: * - A Wildcard and TLD with no root Domain: *.com. - A Wildcard not matching a whole DNS label. e.g. *.foo.com and *.bar.foo.com are valid Wildcards however *bar.foo.com, *-bar.foo.com, and bar*.foo.com are all invalid. Additional notes: A Wildcard will not match empty string. e.g. *.foo.com will match bar.foo.com and baz-bar.foo.com but not .foo.com. The longest Wildcards match first. Only a single virtual host in the entire route configuration can match on *. Also a Domain must be unique across all virtual hosts within an advertise policy. Domains are also used for SNI matching if SNI is activated on the given TCP Load Balancer. Domains also indicate the list of names for which DNS resolution will be automatically resolved to IP addresses by the system.
- `hash_policy_choice` (Attributes) Load Balancing Control Select how the connections are load-balanced<br>Exactly one of `hash_policy_choice_least_active`, `hash_policy_choice_random`, `hash_policy_choice_round_robin`, or `hash_policy_choice_source_ip_stickiness` must be specified when `hash_policy_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--hash_policy_choice))
- `idle_timeout` (Number) Idle timeout The amount of time that a stream can exist without upstream or downstream activity, in milliseconds.<br>**Default:** `3600000`
- `labels` (Map of String) labels Map of string keys and values that can be used to organize and categorize (scope and select) objects as chosen by the user. Values specified here will be used by selector expression
- `service_policy_choice` (Attributes) Service Policies Service policies provide the ability to configure security controls such as IP Allow/Deny lists, Geo IP filtering and Custom rules<br>Exactly one of `active_service_policies`, `no_service_policies`, or `service_policies_from_namespace` must be specified when `service_policy_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--service_policy_choice))
- `sni_default_lb_choice` (Attributes) SNI and Default LB choice This is a choice to enable SNI and default LB options<br>Exactly one of `default_lb_with_sni`, `no_sni`, or `sni` must be specified when `sni_default_lb_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--sni_default_lb_choice))
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

- `provider` (String) Provider Name of the Secret Management Access object that contains information about the store to get encrypted bytes This field needs to be provided only if the url scheme is not string:///




<a id="nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--tls_tcp--tls_certificates_choice--tls_parameters--tls_certificates--ocsp_stapling_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `loadbalancer_type_choice.tls_tcp.tls_certificates_choice.tls_parameters.tls_certificates.ocsp_stapling_choice`

Optional:

- `custom_hash_algorithms` (Attributes) Use Custom Order for Hash Algorithms Use hash algorithms in the custom order. F5XC will try to fetch ocsp response from the CA in the given order. Additionally, LoadBalancer will not become active until ocspResponse cannot be fetched if the certificate has MustStaple extension set.<br>Conflicts with `disable_ocsp_stapling` and `use_system_defaults`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--tls_tcp--tls_certificates_choice--tls_parameters--tls_certificates--ocsp_stapling_choice--custom_hash_algorithms))
- `disable_ocsp_stapling` (Boolean) Disable OCSP Stapling Disable OCSP Stapling. F5XC will not fetch and staple OCSP Response for this certificate. This is the default behavior if no choice is selected.<br>Conflicts with `custom_hash_algorithms` and `use_system_defaults`.
- `use_system_defaults` (Boolean) Fetch with F5XC default settings Use F5XC Default Settings to fetch and staple OCSP Response. OCSP Response will be stapled if it can be fetched. Additionally, LoadBalancer will not become active until ocspResponse cannot be fetched if the certificate has MustStaple extension set. F5XC will try to fetch OCSPResponse with sha256 and sha1 as HashAlgorithm, in that order.<br>Conflicts with `custom_hash_algorithms` and `disable_ocsp_stapling`.

<a id="nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--tls_tcp--tls_certificates_choice--tls_parameters--tls_certificates--ocsp_stapling_choice--custom_hash_algorithms"></a>
### Nested Schema for `loadbalancer_type_choice.tls_tcp.tls_certificates_choice.tls_parameters.tls_certificates.ocsp_stapling_choice.custom_hash_algorithms`

Required:

- `hash_algorithms` (List of String) Hash Algorithms Ordered list of hash algorithms to be used.<br>**Valid Options:** `['SHA1', 'SHA256']` (Multiple selection allowed)

Optional:

- `max_version` (List of String) maximum_protocol_version Maximum TLS protocol version.<br>**Allowed Values (choose one):** `['TLS_AUTO', 'TLSv1_0', 'TLSv1_1', 'TLSv1_2', 'TLSv1_3']`<br>**Default:** `TLS_AUTO`

<a id="nestedatt--origin_pools_weights"></a>
### Nested Schema for `origin_pools_weights`

Required:

- `pool_choice` (Attributes) Pool Choice Select origin pool method, simple origin pool method or more flexible cluster object.<br>Exactly one of `cluster` or `pool` must be specified. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--origin_pools_weights--pool_choice))

Optional:

- `endpoint_subsets` (Map of String) Origin Servers Subset Upstream origin pool may be configured to divide its origin servers into subsets based on metadata attached to the origin servers. Routes may then specify the metadata that a endpoint must match in order to be selected by the load balancer For origin servers which are discovered in K8S or Consul cluster, the label of the service is merged with endpoint's labels. In case of Consul, the label is derived from the 'Tag' field. For labels that are common between configured endpoint and discovered service, labels from discovered service takes precedence. List of key-value pairs that will be used as matching metadata. Only those origin servers of upstream origin pool which match this metadata will be selected for load balancing
- `priority` (Number) Priority Priority of this origin pool, valid only with multiple origin pools. Value of 0 will make the pool as lowest priority origin pool Priority of 1 means highest priority and is considered active. When active origin pool is not available, lower priority origin pools are made active as per the increasing priority.<br>**Default:** `1`
- `weight` (Number) Weight Weight of this origin pool, valid only with multiple origin pool. Value of 0 will disable the pool<br>**Default:** `1`

### Nested Schema for `origin_pools_weights.pool_choice`

- `pool` (Attributes) Pool Simple, commonly used pool parameters with origin pool<br>Conflicts with `cluster`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--origin_pools_weights--pool_choice--pool))

<a id="nestedatt--cluster_retract_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `cluster_retract_choice`

Optional:

- `do_not_retract_cluster` (Boolean) do_not_retract_cluster When this option is configured, cluster with no healthy endpoints is not retracted from route having weighted cluster configuration.<br>Conflicts with `retract_cluster`.
- `retract_cluster` (Boolean) retract_cluster When this option is enabled, weighted cluster will not be considered for load balancing, if all its endpoints are unhealthy. Since the cluster with all unhealthy endpoints is removed, the traffic will be distributed among remaining clusters as per their weight. Also panic-threshold configuration is ignored for retracted cluster. This option is ignored when single destination cluster is configured for route<br>Conflicts with `do_not_retract_cluster`.


<a id="nestedatt--hash_policy_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `hash_policy_choice`

Optional:

- `hash_policy_choice_least_active` (Boolean) Least Active Connections Connections are sent to origin server that has least active connections<br>Conflicts with `hash_policy_choice_random`, `hash_policy_choice_round_robin`, and `hash_policy_choice_source_ip_stickiness`.
- `hash_policy_choice_random` (Boolean) Random Connections are sent to all eligible origin servers in random fashion<br>Conflicts with `hash_policy_choice_least_active`, `hash_policy_choice_round_robin`, and `hash_policy_choice_source_ip_stickiness`.
- `hash_policy_choice_round_robin` (Boolean) Round Robin Connections are sent to all eligible origin servers in round robin fashion<br>Conflicts with `hash_policy_choice_least_active`, `hash_policy_choice_random`, and `hash_policy_choice_source_ip_stickiness`.
- `hash_policy_choice_source_ip_stickiness` (Boolean) Source IP Stickiness Connections are sent to all eligible origin servers using hash of source ip. Consistent hashing algorithm, ring hash, is used to select origin server<br>Conflicts with `hash_policy_choice_least_active`, `hash_policy_choice_random`, and `hash_policy_choice_round_robin`.


<a id="nestedatt--service_policy_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `service_policy_choice`

Optional:

- `active_service_policies` (Attributes) Apply Specified Service Policies Apply the specified list of service policies and bypass the namespace service policy set<br>Conflicts with `no_service_policies` and `service_policies_from_namespace`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--service_policy_choice--active_service_policies))
- `no_service_policies` (Boolean) Do Not Apply Service Policies Do not apply any service policies i.e. bypass the namespace service policy set<br>Conflicts with `active_service_policies` and `service_policies_from_namespace`.
- `service_policies_from_namespace` (Boolean) Apply Namespace Service Policies Apply the active service policies configured as part of the namespace service policy set<br>Conflicts with `active_service_policies` and `no_service_policies`.

<a id="nestedatt--service_policy_choice--active_service_policies"></a>
### Nested Schema for `service_policy_choice.active_service_policies`

Required:

- `policies` (Attributes List) policies Service Policies is a sequential engine where policies (and rules within the policy) are evaluated one after the other. It's important to define the correct order (policies evaluated from top to bottom in the list) for service policies, to get the intended result. For each request, its characteristics are evaluated based on the match criteria in each service policy starting at the top. If there is a match in the current policy, then the policy takes effect, and no more policies are evaluated. Otherwise, the next policy is evaluated. If all policies are evaluated and none match, then the request will be denied by default. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--service_policy_choice--active_service_policies--policies))

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an `import` block to import this resource by ID.

> **Note:** Replace placeholder values (for example, `<namespace>`, `<name>`) with actual values.

#### Command-Line Import

Use the following `command` to import this resource from the command line:

```shell
terraform import f5xc_tcp_loadbalancer.example <namespace>/<name>
```

#### HCL Import Block

Use the following `hcl` block to import this resource during `plan` or `apply`:

```hcl
import {
	id = "<namespace>/<name>"
	to = f5xc_tcp_loadbalancer.example
}
```
